chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, good character (al-khuluq) is a gift that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants to His creation. From it is natural disposition (sajjiyyah), and from it is intention (niyyah). So I said, 'Which of the two is superior?' He said: 'The one with the natural disposition is innate and cannot choose otherwise, while the one with intention is patient in obedience with patience; therefore, he is superior of the two.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between natural good character and acquired good character in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is drawn between innate temperament (sajjiyyah) and deliberate spiritual striving (niyyah), with the latter deemed superior due to the virtue of patience (sabr) in worship. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of effort over mere natural endowment, reflecting the concept of 'fada'il al-a'mal' (excellence of deeds). The hadith underscores that moral excellence is not just a gift but a cultivated state achieved through conscious discipline.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The (good) manners are a Grant Granted by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic to His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. So, from it is the natural disposition, and from it is the intention’. So I said, ‘So which of the two is superior?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(As for) the one with the natural disposition, he is naturally disposed, not having the capacity for something else; while the one with the intention is patient upon the obedience with an excellent patience, therefore he is superior of the two’.
en.sarwar: 11. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Imam said, ‘Moral behavior is a gift that, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, bestows upon His creature. From moral behavior comes habit and intentions.’ 1 then asked, ‘Which one is better?’ The Imam said, ‘A person with an established habit is not able to do anything else. The person who possesses the intention may exercise patience for worship and thus, is the better one of the two.’”
